items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Interviewer asks: 'Isn't she Jackie and Roy's daughter? Do you know?' Interviewee responds: 'Could be.'

ctx.x: No, he was the manager, right?

He was the manager. Whoever. Jimmy asked Paul. He remembers it as Barbra had her own pianist, but Barbra tells – Barbra I don’t think remembers any of it, because what happened was, I’m reading the New Yorker, which I had boycotted, because they had that picture of Obama and his wife looking like terrorists. So I cancelled my subscription. I thought, wrong. After about eight months, I gave up and I went back to the New Yorker. I’m reading the New Yorker. It’s like a Thursday. Barbra Streisand is coming to the…

First of all, it’s not true. She never even – I know the story, right? So I ask our p.r. person. I said, “Look,” . . . . First I called the Village Vanguard. “Lorraine [Gordon]. I’m Jimmy Cobb’s wife.” She says, “Yes, dear, I know Jimmy Cobb.” I said, “Lorraine, Saturday.” She says, “Call me Monday, dear.” “It’s Saturday, Lorraine.” “Call me Monday.” So she gives me to Jed, the door guy. He tells me to call Marty Erlichman, who is the manager. So I decide I’m not going to call. I’ll get our p.r. person to call.…
